sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 of the two-sheet 1925 Sanborn atlas of Waldwick, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points roughly to the right. It covers the centre of the borough on both sides of the Erie Railroad main line, which crosses the sheet diagonally with the Waldwick passenger station on its south side and a group of sidings by the Waldwick Coal & Lumber Co. yard on Cleveland Avenue. North of the tracks the grid of Wanamaker, Cleveland and Maple avenues is crossed by Wycoff Avenue, Conklin, Wagner and Prospect; Hohokus Creek and a brook run along the top edge past the Waldwick Bleachery Co. works and its water tower, and the Katterman-Mitchell Co. silk weaving mill stands on Wanamaker Avenue. The 1st Reformed Church is at the top of Prospect. South of the tracks the small business centre on Prospect and Lafayette Place holds stores, a post office, the Orvil Hotel and a pool room; further south lie Harrison and Lyrington avenues, the right of way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. electric line, the Waldwick Public School and the fire department on Prospect, and Franklin Avenue running diagonally to the junction with Wycoff Avenue, where the Waldwick M.E. Church and Sunday school stand. The east side shows Hewson Avenue, Frederick, Chestnut and the start of the Waldwick Improvement Co. tract on Grove, Waldwick Avenue and Central Avenue. Housing is almost entirely frame dwellings on narrow numbered lots, many still vacant. The sheet carries the title cartouche (population 1400), notes on water facilities and the fire department, the legend and a small location map of New Jersey; the last two are left out of the mask.
notes: Wycoff Av. is today Wyckoff Avenue; Franklin Av. is Franklin Turnpike.
Prospect north of Franklin Av. is today West Prospect Street.
Cleveland Av. east of Prospect is today Zazzetti Street; west of Prospect it keeps the name Cleveland Avenue.
Chestnut is today Walter Nightingale Place.
Lyrington Av. appears to be today's Walter Hammond Place (its east end at Prospect matched to 1.3 m); the modern street bends to Wyckoff Avenue where the sheet shows no street.
Maple Av. ends at the railroad on the sheet; the modern Maple Avenue / West Prospect Street junction is not drawn.
Elkton Ct. is marked 'arbitrary' and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Works: Waldwick Bleachery Co.; Katterman-Mitchell Co. silk mill; Waldwick Coal & Lumber Co.; Erie R.R. passenger station.

sheet-2-1.description: Main part of sheet 2 of the 1925 Sanborn atlas of Waldwick, at 100 feet to an inch and turned like sheet 1 so that north points roughly to the right. It continues sheet 1 to the east. At the top left are Smith, Clinton Place, Bennett Street or Washington Place and the east end of Cleveland Avenue beside a brook, then the Erie Railroad main line with a signal tower and, curving away from it, the line of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. on its own right of way between Hewson and Harrison avenues. Below, Franklin Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally with a garage at Park Place; North runs off it to the north. The south and east half is the platted Waldwick Improvement Co. and Waldwick Park tracts: long rows of narrow numbered lots along Waldwick Avenue, Lincoln Place, Bergen Avenue, Cottage Place and Highwood Avenue, crossed by Central Avenue and Summit Avenue. Only a scattering of one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto houses stands on them; several streets are marked not opened. Chestnut and the south end of Hewson Avenue are at the left edge where the sheet meets sheet 1. The right third of the lower sheet is blank apart from the scale bar; the top right holds two separately framed insets (parts 2 and 3).
notes: Franklin Av. is today Franklin Turnpike; Chestnut is Walter Nightingale Place; North is North Street; Park Pl. is Park Avenue.
Bennett St. or Washington Pl. is today Bohnert Place; Cleveland Av. here is today Zazzetti Street.
Cottage Pl. is today part of Summit Avenue, which turns south at the old Summit Av. / Cottage Pl. corner.
A note at Smith gives Hopper St. 485 ft beyond (see the detachment at right).

Sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch, turned like sheet 1. Three parts: part 1 main map (Franklin Av east of Chestnut, Waldwick Improvement Co. tract: Waldwick Av, Lincoln Pl, Bergen Av, Cottage Pl, Highwood Av, Central and Summit Av; Clinton Pl, Bennett St or Washington Pl, Smith at top left); part 2 inset top right (Will A. Sharp Add'n: Irving Pl, Harrison Pl, Hopper Av, Sherman, Pennington, Alexander Av); part 3 small inset of the Waldwick Water Works at Hopper Av and Prospect.

sheet-2-2.description: Inset at the top right of sheet 2 of the 1925 Sanborn atlas of Waldwick, framed by a heavy line and drawn at the sheet's 100 feet to an inch, turned like the main sheet so that north points to the right. It shows the Will A. Sharp Add'n, a small grid west of the main village: Irving Place and Harrison Place crossing Sherman Avenue, Pennington Avenue and Alexander Avenue, with Hopper Avenue along the foot of the inset. The blocks are cut into numbered building lots, most still vacant, with a few one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto houses, mainly along Hopper Avenue and Pennington Avenue. Water pipes of 6 inches run along the avenues, and a fire alarm box stands at Hopper and Pennington. The inset also carries the sheet's date stamp (March 1925) and the scale note for the entire sheet.
notes: All six streets keep their names today.

sheet-2-3.description: Small framed inset on sheet 2 of the 1925 Sanborn atlas of Waldwick showing the Waldwick Water Works at the corner of Hopper Avenue and Prospect, west of the village. A single concrete-block pump house stands on the head race of a stream, with the tail race passing under Prospect; an 8 inch water pipe runs from it along Prospect. The notes say the works runs continuously and that the supply is from three wells with two Gould 8 by 10 inch triplex pumps driven by water or electric power. A note gives 900 feet along Prospect to the 1st Reformed Church, which is on sheet 1. The inset is drawn at the sheet's 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points roughly to the right, as its arrow shows.
notes: Prospect here is today West Prospect Street.
Placed from the one junction Hopper Avenue / West Prospect Street with the scale of part 1 assumed; low confidence.
